legend.title: Legend
legend.close: Orange vessel: close, but no risk of collision
legend.wake: Wake: share of polar speed (green ≥ 95 %, yellow 80–95 %, red < 80 %)
legend.ghost: Ghost boat: where the polar speed would put you
legend.danger: Red vessel: risk of collision and you must keep clear
legend.cpa: Line to the closest point of approach
legend.giveWay: Your boat all orange + banner: you must give way (rules of the road)
legend.trim: Trim cars and tiller (accent colour): positions to read
legend.loads: Sheets, vang and backstay: load, green (eased) to red (hard on)
legend.isochrones: Isochrones: where you will be in 5, 10, 15 min on each heading (polar, wind, current); dot: current heading
legend.yields: Violet vessel: risk of collision, it must keep clear of you (arrow: its expected turn)

replay.title: Replay
replay.explain: Voyages recorded on this display (every 5 s under way). Replay one to watch it again in the 3D view, accelerated.
replay.none: No voyage recorded yet. They appear here after a first outing.

manual.online: The online manual, always for the latest version. It opens in a new tab and needs an internet connection.

offline.title: Offline data
offline.explain: With internet (marina, 4G), download the bathymetry and the wind forecast around the boat: the 3D view will use them at sea without a network. SHOM surveys (5 to 20 m) are kept by the boat's server for every display. Charts already viewed are kept as you go; for a full offline chart, add MBTiles charts to the Signal K server (used automatically).
offline.shomTitle: SHOM bathymetry on the boat's server
offline.shomNone: No SHOM survey around the boat.
offline.shomNo7z: Install 7z on the server (apt install p7zip-full) to extract the surveys.
offline.shomCredit: Source: SHOM digital elevation models, Licence Ouverte. Depths relative to chart datum.

start.title: First steps
start.intro: Ocearo shows your boat, the sea and the traffic in live 3D from the data of a Signal K server. Five things to know before casting off.

connect.title: Connect to Signal K
connect.text: Installed on the boat's Signal K server, Ocearo connects to it on its own. Opened from elsewhere, enter the server address in System › Settings (for example 192.168.1.10:3000, or demo.signalk.org to try).

demo.title: Demo mode
demo.text: Without a server, demo mode (System › Settings) fills the screens with sample values. Turn it off as soon as you sail with real data: the sample values would mix with yours.

views.title: Boat view, split view, full view
views.text: The Apps menu switches between the 3D view alone, the 3D view beside a page (dashboard, chart, logbook…) and the page alone. Your choice is kept on the next start.

phone.title: On a phone
phone.text: The bottom bar keeps the essentials: System, Voice, MOB, the readings and the Apps menu, which holds the chart, weather, dashboard and help. Add Ocearo to the home screen for a full-screen app.

settings.title: Make it yours
settings.text: In Settings: your boat model and its polars, units, theme (day, dark, red night, or automatic by the sun), the HUD style, the AIS alert distances and the links to your chart and instrument apps.

view.title: 3D view
view.intro: The main screen: your boat in 3D, the values you need now, and the sea around you. Tap a number to see what it shows.

toolbar.title: Modes and layers
toolbar.text: Sailing, anchor watch and harbour modes, then the theme, the sea (black, 3D water, chart, bathymetry, weather), the polar rings and laylines, and the AIS traffic. A dot under a button means it is on.

speed.title: Speed
speed.text: The large number is your speed. Tap it to switch between speed over ground (SOG), velocity made good (VMG), speed through water (STW) and the share of the polar speed.

values.title: Values of the mode
values.text: Heading, wind, apparent angle and distance to the waypoint while sailing; position, swing and alarm radius at anchor; the docking values in the harbour.

legend.title: Legend
legend.text: Opens the meaning of every colour and ribbon of the scene. The last section of this guide lists them too.

sky.title: Sun, UV, time, battery
sky.text: Next sunrise or sunset, the UV index, the boat's time (GPS) and the house battery. Tap the battery to switch to the tanks.

sails.title: Sails and trim
sails.text: The sails follow the wind angle. Telltales, draft ("Depth 11%") and the car positions help trim; sheets and backstay turn from green to red with the load.

ais.title: AIS traffic
ais.text: Ships and boats within 5 km, at their real place and heading. Tap one for its name, distance, closest point of approach (CPA, TCPA), speed and course.

compass.title: Compass and wind
compass.text: The rose turns with the heading. Arrows on its edge give the true and apparent wind with their speeds; the marks show the laylines and the course to the waypoint.

wake.title: Wake
wake.text: Coloured by the share of the polar speed you reach: green 95 % and more, yellow 80 to 95 %, red below.

depth.title: Depth
depth.text: Depth now and over the last 10 minutes, red when shallow, with the rate it is shoaling. On a phone it is a gauge at the bottom.

tide.title: Tide
tide.text: Height now, rising or falling, the day's curve, next high and low water and the coefficient. On a phone it is a gauge at the bottom.

bottom.title: System, voice, MOB
bottom.text: System opens the settings. Voice sets what the Ocearo assistant may say (everything, safety only, silence). The red ring is the man-overboard button.

readings.title: Readings
readings.text: Temperatures, pressure, humidity and air quality. Tap a reading to see the next one.

shortcuts.title: Pages
shortcuts.text: Chart, weather, Apps menu, dashboard and this help. On a phone or a small tablet they are all in the Apps menu.

route.title: Route and performance
route.intro: With a waypoint and your polars, the scene shows where you are going and how fast you could get there.

toggles.title: Polar rings and laylines
toggles.text: The compass button shows the polar rings (with the black sea), the ruler button the laylines.

waypoint.title: Distance to the waypoint
waypoint.text: From the active route of your chart plotter or Signal K.

route.title: Route
route.text: The blue chevron ribbon leads to the next waypoint.

isochrones.title: Polar rings
isochrones.text: Where you would be in 5, 10 and 15 minutes on each heading, from your polar, the wind and the current. The dot is your present heading.

laylines.title: Laylines
laylines.text: The tacks that reach the waypoint: red on port tack, green on starboard.

wake.title: Performance
wake.text: The wake colour tells how much of the polar speed you are making.

traffic.title: Traffic and rules of the road
traffic.intro: Each AIS target is coloured by what the rules of the road expect, and Ocearo tells you when you must keep clear.

toggle.title: AIS
toggle.text: Shows or hides the traffic (also at anchor and in the harbour).

banner.title: You must give way
banner.text: Your hull turns orange and this banner names the vessel and the rule. Act early and clearly.

yields.title: They keep clear
yields.text: Violet: risk of collision, the other vessel must give way; the arrow shows the manoeuvre expected from it. Keep your course and speed, and watch.

tags.title: Labels
tags.text: Name or type, who keeps clear and the rule (12, 13, 15, 18…).

danger.title: We keep clear
danger.text: Red: risk of collision and it is up to you. Orange: close but no risk. White: no risk.

advice.title: Advice
advice.text: A suggested course change, or slowing down when no turn clears every vessel. Advice only: you remain the skipper.

anchor.title: Anchor watch
anchor.intro: At anchor, Ocearo draws the swing circle and the alarm radius around the anchor, and shows the boat's track.

button.title: Anchor mode
button.text: Switches to the anchor watch. The anchor position and the alarm radius come from the server (ocearo-core or the anchor alarm plugin); until the anchor is set, the circle is centred on the boat.

position.title: Position and time
position.text: For the logbook or a call on the radio.

values.title: Wind, swing, alarm radius
values.text: True wind speed, distance from the anchor, and the radius beyond which the alarm sounds.

alarm.title: Alarm circle
alarm.text: Coloured when the boat drags out of it; the server's anchor alarm sounds and the voice assistant warns you.

swing.title: Swing circle
swing.text: The space your boat sweeps with the scope paid out.

track.title: Track
track.text: Where the boat has been since anchoring: a track spreading out means dragging.

anchorPoint.title: Anchor
anchorPoint.text: The anchor position and the rode from the bow.

parking.title: Harbour
parking.intro: Like a car's parking view: your predicted path, the berth you aim at, and guidance to come alongside.

button.title: Harbour mode
button.text: A top view close to the boat, for manoeuvring in the marina.

berth.title: Virtual berth
berth.text: The berth you aim at, placed ahead of the boat.

path.title: Predicted path
path.text: Where the boat goes with the present rudder and speed.

wind.title: Wind
wind.text: True and apparent wind arrows: what pushes you off or onto the pontoon.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.text: Lined up, too far left or right, distance to the entrance.

types.title: Berth type
types.text: Bow-in, stern-in, alongside, mooring buoy, or place the berth ahead.

bathymetry.title: Bathymetry
bathymetry.intro: The sea floor in relief around you, coloured by depth, with the chart laid over it.

button.title: Sea mode
button.text: This button cycles through black, 3D water, chart, bathymetry and weather.

coast.title: Coast
coast.text: The land in relief on the horizon.

soundings.title: Soundings
soundings.text: Depths in metres from the SHOM data (France), downloaded by ocearo-core.

seabed.title: Seabed
seabed.text: Relief and colour by depth: the lighter, the shallower.

keel.title: Under the keel
keel.text: The line down to the bottom with the depth straight below the boat.

weather.title: Weather
weather.intro: The forecast wind over the chart, like Windy (Open-Meteo forecast, needs internet).

button.title: Weather mode
button.text: Same sea button, on the weather setting.

slider.title: Forecast time
slider.text: Slide to see the wind in the coming hours; the colour scale gives the speed in knots.

map.title: Chart
map.text: The map under the wind, for the coast and the harbours.

wind.title: Wind
wind.text: Streaks show the direction, colours the strength.

mob.title: Man overboard
mob.intro: One press marks the position. Ocearo shows the person's estimated drift and the way back.

button.title: MOB button
button.text: Marks the position, raises the alarm on every screen and starts the timer.

alert.title: Alert
alert.text: Time elapsed, distance and bearing to the person. Acknowledge stops the sound; Go to MOB sets the person as the destination when the server offers the course API.

marker.title: Estimated position
marker.text: Where the person should be now, with the time and distance.

drift.title: Drift
drift.text: From the drop point, carried by the current and the wind.

return.title: Way back
return.text: The route to the estimated position.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.intro: Beside the 3D view: the traffic as a radar, the weather and the course.

view.title: 3D view
view.text: Stays live on the left in split view.

radar.title: AIS radar
radar.text: Targets around you, the closest first, with their names.

tactical.title: Closest vessels
tactical.text: Distance and closest point of approach (CPA) of each.

weather.title: Weather
weather.text: Conditions now and the forecast wind.

course.title: Course
course.text: Distance and bearing to the waypoint, cross-track error and VMG.

logbook.title: Logbook
logbook.intro: The logbook kept on the boat's server by ocearo-core: automatic entries for alerts and AIS encounters, your own entries, and the voyages.

tabs.title: Tabs
tabs.text: Timeline, entries, fleet, and past voyages (replay one in the 3D view).

add.title: New entry
add.text: Add an entry by hand, or let the assistant write one from the present data.

entries.title: Entries
entries.text: Time, course, speed, weather, pressure, depth, position, log, engine hours and the note.

legend.title: Legend
legend.intro: What the colours, ribbons and bands of the 3D view mean.
